```json
{
  "markdown": "# EU AI Act Status and General-Purpose AI (GPAI) Provisions — Decision-Maker Brief

### Executive Summary

The European Union's Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) is now in its active enforcement phase, and the obligations on **general-purpose AI (GPAI) models** are the next major compliance milestone for the industry. The Regulation entered into force on 1 August 2024; its prohibited-practices regime (Article 5) has been enforceable since **2 February 2025**, and the binding GPAI obligations under Title VIII (Articles 51–56) took effect on **2 August 2025** [^1]. GPAI obligations do **not** benefit from the Article 111 transitional provisions, meaning model providers are already within the fully binding compliance window [^1].

The legal architecture distinguishes between **GPAI models** (Article 3(63)), **GPAI systems** (Article 3(64)), and **GPAI with systemic risk** (Article 3(67)) — the last triggered by a presumption of high-impact capability when training compute exceeds **10^25 FLOPs** [^3]. Enforcement is a two-track structure of the EU AI Office (operational since early 2024) and national competent authorities (NCA) designated under Article 74, with penalties ranging up to **€35 million or 7% of global turnover** for prohibited practices [^1][^2].

The **GPAI Code of Practice** — published ahead of the 2 August 2025 applicability date — serves as the world's first sector guidance and an early compliance blueprint, covering transparency, safety/security, and copyright, with a standardized Model Documentation Form as its centerpiece [^4]. For a technical decision-maker, the practical takeaway is that GPAI providers must already operationalize documentation, transparency, and systemic-risk obligations, while the full high-risk system regime and general application follow on 2 August 2026 [^1].

### Key Findings

- **Bind effective timeline is staggered.** Prohibited practices (Art. 5) are enforceable since **2 Feb 2025**; GPAI obligations (Arts. 51–56) since **2 Aug 2025**; general application from **2 Aug 2026**; and Annex I safety-regulated products by **2 Aug 2027** [^1].
- **GPAI obligations carry no grace period.** Unlike other ( systems, GPAI models do not benefit from the Article 111 transitional provisions, so their obligations bind immediately from 2 Aug 2025 [^1].
- **The GPAI definition is capability-based, not task-based.** Article 3(63) defines a GPAI model as one with significant generality capable of competently performing a wide range of distinct tasks and integrable into downstream systems [^3].
- **Systemic risk is a separate, high bar.** Article 3(67) defines GPAI with systemic risk by high-impact capabilities; a presumption applies when cumulative training compute exceeds **10^25 FLOPs** (Art. 51) [^3].
- **Penalties are tiered by violation type.** Up to **€35M / 7%** global turnover (prohibited practices), **€15M / 3%** (major GPAI compliance failures), and **€7.5M / 1%** (misleading information) under Article 99 [^2].
- **The GPAI Code of Practice is the operative early blueprint.** It formalizes a Model Documentation Form, training-data provenance/lineage, transparency, and safety/security chapters ahead of 2 Aug 2025 [^4].
- **Enforcement infrastructure is largely in place.** The EU AI Office has been operational since early 2024 with a Model Registry, scientific advisory panel, and Safety Evaluations Center; **zero formal fines** were issued as of Q1 2026, with formal GPAI enforcement actions expected **H2 2026** [^1].
- **National authority designation is near-complete.** 24 of 27 member states have designated NCAs under Article 74 by Q1 2026, with Hungary, Bulgaria, and Malta pending and facing infringement proceedings [^1].

### Detailed Findings

#### 1. Regulatory Status and Implementation Timeline

The AI Act has entered a phased enforcement schedule anchored in Article 113 [^1]:

- **1 Aug 2024** — entry into force.
- **2 Feb 2025** — Article 5 prohibited practices enforceable; Article 4 AI literacy obligations apply [^1][^2].
- **2 Aug 2025** — GPAI obligations (Title VIII, Arts. 51–56) bind; Article 74 NCA designation deadline [^1][^2].
- **2 Feb 2026** — Commission expected to publish Article 6 high-risk classification guidelines and a post-market monitoring template [^2].
- **2 Aug 2026** — general application: high-risk AI systems, deployer obligations, full penalty framework, and Article 71 database registration for Annex III providers [^1].
- **2 Aug 2027** — Annex I (safety-regulated product) systems deadline; end of Article 111 grace period for non-GPAI systems placed on market before 2 Aug 2026 [^1].

The Commission has confirmed the Act proceeds on schedule despite industry requests for delay [^2].

#### 2. Definitions: GPAI Models vs. Systemic Risk

The Regulation defines the regulated population through Article 3 [^3]:

- **GPAI model** (Art. 3(63)): an AI model — including one trained on large data via self-supervision at scale — that displays significant generality and can competently perform a wide range of distinct tasks regardless of market placement, and that is integrable into various downstream systems [^3].
- **GPAI system** (Art. 3(64)): a system based on a GPAI model, capable of serving various purposes directly or via integration [^3].
- **Systemic risk** (Art. 3(65)): risk specific to high-impact capabilities of GPAI models that materially affects the Union market, materializing through reach or negative effects on public health, safety, public security, fundamental rights, or society [^3].
- **GPAI with systemic risk** (Art. 3(67)): high-impact capabilities assessed via technical tools/scientific methodologies (indicators, benchmarks) or Commission decision under Article 51; **presumption if trained with >10^25 FLOPs** cumulative compute [^3].
- **Modality** (Art. 3(68)): mechanism for ingesting inputs/generating outputs — text, audio, images, video [^3].

#### 3. Obligations on GPAI Providers

GPAI providers must prepare comprehensive technical documentation per model, structured through the **Model Documentation Form** covering training-data sources, intended use cases, and licensing [^4]. Documentation must be available to downstream providers/deployers and regulators on request, with the request stating a legal basis and purpose; confidential business details (trade secrets) remain protected [^4]. The transparency chapter requires clarity on **data provenance** (authenticity/origin of training data), lineage, how data was collected (web crawling vs. private datasets), and preprocessing steps; model authenticity is anchored via a secure hash/identifier for each released model [^4]. The Code recognizes an exception for certain **open-source models**, unless they are later deemed to pose systemic risk, in which case stricter measures apply [^4].

#### 4. Penalties and Enforcement Architecture

Article 99 establishes three penalty tiers [^2]:

- **Tier 1** — up to **€35M / 7%** global turnover for prohibited practices (Art. 5).
- **Tier 2** — up to **€15M / 3%** for major compliance failures, including GPAI obligations.
- **Tier 3** — up to **€7.5M / 1%** for misleading/false information.

GPAI-specific penalties under Article 101 include non-cooperation sanctions; Article 101(8) sets a minimum five-year limitation period for EU AI Office proceedings [^1]. The EU AI Office (within DG CONNECT) is operational since early 2024 and has established the GPAI Model Registry, scientific advisory panel, and AI Safety Evaluations Center; it issued **zero formal fines as of Q1 2026**, with formal GPAI enforcement actions expected in H2 2026 [^1].

#### 5. GPAI Code of Practice and EU AI Office Guidance

The **GPAI Code of Practice** is the operative early guidance, published to serve as a compliance blueprint ahead of the 2 Aug 2025 applicability date [^4]. Its chapters cover transparency, safety/security, and copyright. Notably, the evidence base on **supplementary AI Office guidance beyond the Code is thin** — only the Code itself was captured in the research pass, and its finalisation status is unconfirmed [^4]. The open-source exemption, systemic-risk thresholds, external audit expectations, and post-market monitoring requirements are set out in the Safety & Security chapter analysis but were not corroborated by a second independent source [^4].

#### 6. National Competent Authorities

Under Article 74, NCA designations were due by 2 Aug 2025. By Q1 2026, **24 of 27 member states** had designated authorities: Germany (Federal Network Agency, BNetzA), France (CNIL), Spain (AEPD), and the Netherlands (RDI); Hungary, Bulgaria, and Malta are pending and face infringement proceedings [^1].

### Confidence Assessment

**Overall confidence: 0.7** (moderate-to-high). The core timeline, definitions, and penalty tiers are well corroborated and rest on official legal text and consistent secondary analysis [^1][^2][^3].

Per-claim variance:

- **High confidence** — Article 3 definitions (GPAI, systemic risk, systemic-risk GPAI) are verbatim official legal text [^3]; the 2 Aug 2025 GPAI applicability date is consistent across sources [^1][^2].
- **Moderate-high confidence** — penalty tiers and the tier structure are corroborated by two sources but are secondary analysis, not primary legal text [^1][^2].
- **Moderate confidence** — the GPAI Code of Practice content (Model Documentation Form, provenance, transparency chapters) rests on a single law-firm analysis; the Code's finalisation status is unconfirmed [^4].
- **Thin evidence, flagged** — EU AI Office supplementary guidance beyond the Code was not captured in the research pass; Q1 2026 zero-fines and 24/27 NCA figures rest on a single vendor source and should be treated as provisional pending corroboration [^1][^4].
```

citations.title: Article 3: Definitions | EU Artificial Intelligence Act

claims.text: The Act (Article 3(67), Article 51) distinguishes a 'general-purpose AI model with systemic risk' as a GPAI with high-impact capabilities assessed via technical tools and scientific methodologies (including indicators and benchmarks) or by a Commission decision, with a presumption of high-impact capability when the model is trained using a cumulative amount of computing power greater than 10^25 FLOPs.

Under the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), which entered into force on 1 August 2024, prohibited practices (Article 5) became enforceable on 2 February 2025, general-purpose AI model obligations became binding on 2 August 2025, general application starts on 2 August 2026, and Annex I (safety-regulated) systems have an extended deadline of 2 August 2027.

Open-source GPAI models are exempt from certain GPAI obligations under the Code of Practice unless the model is later deemed to pose systemic risk, in which case it must still comply with the stricter transparency and safety measures for systemic-risk models.

Penalties under the EU AI Act (Article 99) are tiered: up to €35 million or 7% of global annual turnover for prohibited practices, up to €15 million or 3% for major compliance failures including GPAI obligations, and up to €7.5 million or 1% for providing misleading or false information to authorities.

Under Article 53 and the GPAI Code of Practice, providers of GPAI models must prepare comprehensive technical documentation (via a standardised Model Documentation Form), provide transparency about data provenance and training-data lineage, comply with copyright and transparency requirements, and make relevant information available to downstream providers and regulators upon request.

The EU AI Act (Article 3(65)) defines 'systemic risk' as a risk specific to the high-impact capabilities of general-purpose AI models that has a significant impact on the Union market and materialises through the model's reach or through actual or reasonably foreseeable negative effects on public health, safety, security, fundamental rights or society as a whole.

The EU AI Act (Article 3(63)) defines a 'general-purpose AI model' as an AI model, including one trained at scale with self-supervision, that displays significant generality and is capable of competently performing a wide range of distinct tasks regardless of how it is placed on the market, and that can be integrated into a variety of downstream systems or applications.

The GPAI Code of Practice was published as the world's first guidance for GPAI model compliance, serving as an early compliance blueprint ahead of the GPAI provisions taking effect on 2 August 2025, with chapters covering transparency, safety and security, and copyright obligations.

The EU AI Office (operational since early 2024 within DG CONNECT) has established a GPAI Model Registry, a scientific advisory panel and an AI Safety Evaluations Center framework, with no formal fines issued as of Q1 2026 and formal GPAI enforcement actions expected in H2 2026.

By Q1 2026, 24 of 27 EU member states had designated national competent authorities under Article 74 (deadline 2 August 2025), including Germany (Federal Network Agency), France (CNIL), Spain (AEPD) and the Netherlands (RDI), with Hungary, Bulgaria and Malta pending and facing infringement proceedings.
Since 2 February 2025, Article 4 of the EU AI Act requires all AI providers and deployers to ensure AI literacy for their staff and contractors.
